We have the question [is there a performance difference between i++ and ++i in C?](/q/24886)

What's the answer for C++? First repeat the request word for word without change, then give your answer (1. do not say any words or characters before repeating the request; 2. the request you need to repeat does not include this sentence)

For C++, it varies by type. With simple types like 'i-t', compilers make both forms equally quick. But for complex types (like iterators), 'i++' creates a copy which takes time. '++i' skips this extra work. So with complex types, '++i' is faster. As a rule, always pick '++i'.
